newsitem.title: USA: Bayer gets FDA okay on cholesterol drug.
newsitem.headline: Bayer gets FDA okay on cholesterol drug.

text.p: Bayer Corp, a unit of Bayer AG, said Friday that Baycol (cerivastatin sodium), a new cholesterol-lowering agent, has been cleared for marketing by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

Baycol is an HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor, or statin, indicated as an adjunct to diet for patients with primary hypercholesterolemia and mixed dyslipidemia (Fredrickson types IIa and IIb) who have not responded adequately to dietary restrictions and other non-pharmacological measures.
Cerivastatin is currently marketed in the United Kingdom and Bayer said it expects regulatory clearances for cerivastatin in several other major markets of the world throughout 1997.
